title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 66-68 of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes). M is a finite poset of cells (X ≤ Y meaning X lies in the closure of Y; X̄ is the closed star below X). M carries a symmetric 'separation' relation ∥. From it Grothendieck defines polar-type operators. cosupp°(A) = {Y | Y ∥ X for all X ∈ A}, and supp° is the associated closure operator. A 'support' is a subset closed for this Galois connection, i.e. a set of the form cosupp°(A). The previous page treated the trivial case ∥ = '≠', where every subset is a support.

This page starts with the second example, X ∥ Y ⇔ X̄ ∩ Ȳ = ∅ (closures disjoint). Here the supports are certain ≤-closed subsets of M, of a rather special kind. Grothendieck remarks that he does not see how to express them in terms of 'internal' supports.

He then names Σ_M ("notation standard") the set of supports, ordered by inclusion, and lists its structure:
- It has least element ∅ and greatest element M.
- Arbitrary infima exist and are set-theoretic intersections, so Σ_M is a closure system and hence a complete lattice.
- The map S ↦ ∁S (the polar/orthocomplement S ↦ cosupp°(S), not the set complement) is an order-reversing involution ('antiinvolution') of Σ_M.
- That map exchanges Inf and Sup, so Sup S_i = supp°(∪ S_i), the closure of the union. He warns explicitly not to confuse this with ∪ S_i.

Finally, for a subset L ⊂ M he restricts the relation, ∥_L = ∥_M on L. This gives Σ_L, and he looks for a canonical map Σ_M → Σ_L. The next page makes this map S ↦ S ∩ L, proves it lands in Σ_L under a genericity hypothesis using the 'shadow' omb°, and builds a map in the opposite direction.

In modern terms: the polar lattice of an orthogonality space (M, ∥), which is a complete ortholattice when ∥ is irreflexive. This serves the 1986 project of a combinatorial/tame 'analysis situs' of cell complexes, where supports play the role of closed sets.
errors: The symbol ∁S must be read as the polar/orthocomplement (cosupp°) of S, not the set-theoretic complement. The set complement of a support is not a support in general (in the disjoint-closure example the complement of a ≤-closed set is not ≤-closed). With that reading the claims hold: the polar is an involutive order-reversing bijection on closed sets because ∥ is symmetric.
The first line is fragmentary. The sentence about expressing supports via 'supports internes' is incomplete and the claim is left unexplained.
Σ_L is introduced but the compatibility of restriction with supports is not justified on this page. The next page shows it needs an extra genericity hypothesis.

ideas.what: Supports = closed sets of the Galois connection induced by a symmetric relation ∥ on the cell poset; Σ_M is a complete lattice with Inf = intersection and Sup = closure of the union
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois lattice (formal concept lattice), lattice of closed sets of a closure operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1940, polarities); Ore (1944); Wille (1982, formal concept analysis)

ideas.what: The polar S ↦ S^⊥ is an order-reversing involution of Σ_M exchanging Inf and Sup
ideas.modern_name: Orthocomplementation on the complete ortholattice of an orthogonality space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (orthogonality spaces); Birkhoff–von Neumann lineage

ideas.what: For ∥ = disjointness of closures, supports are special closed sets and the join is not the union
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial analogue of regular closed/regular open sets (join = closure of union, as in Tarski's regular-open algebra)

ideas.what: Restricting ∥ to a subset L to get Σ_L and seeking a comparison map Σ_M → Σ_L
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of polar lattices under restriction of orthogonality spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'supports' attached to a cell complex via the relation 'closures disjoint' form exactly the ortholattice of an orthogonality space. This is a discrete analogue of the regular-closed-set algebra. The tame-topology notes thus implicitly connect cellular analysis situs with orthogonality-space / regular-open-algebra theory; no published development of this link for cell complexes is known to me.
missed.quote: Sup S_i = supp°(∪ S_i). On prendra bien garde de ne pas le confondre avec ∪ S_i.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It could interest work on mereotopology / region connection calculi and discrete topology, which study exactly such 'contact' relations and their Boolean or ortho lattices. Mathematically, though, it is standard lattice theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up the standard Galois/polar lattice of a symmetric relation on a cell poset: closure system, orthocomplement, Sup as closure of union. This is routine lattice theory, interesting only as a document of Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial approach to tame topology.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely begins 'travaille avec la relation' (continuing 'Si on' from the previous page) rather than 'transitive avec la relation'.
Line 3: 'si bien particulières' is probably 'assez/bien particulières'.
Lines 3-5: 'Je ne vois pas [comment] elles ne se pourraient exprimer dans supports internes' is a garbled reading; the sense is 'I do not see how to express them in terms of internal supports!'.
'Il a des Inf quelconques — ce sont les ∩ ensemblistes —' followed by 'ment' is likely a fragment of a word such as 'évidemment'.
'Σ_L, avec ∥_L = ∥_L sur L' should presumably read ∥_L = ∥_M restricted to L. The struck word after 'On' is followed by inserted 'voudrait' ('On voudrait une application canonique').
In 'S → ∁S' a crossed-out symbol precedes ∁ in the image.
